correctness.rationale: For an isometric reference, the normalized difference has unit norm. The exact spherical-cap elementary optimization yields a lower bound s times every output increment. A rank-two skew contraction J, chosen on a plane containing one reference increment, has Lipschitz norm one, zero limiting radius and finite cap radius s. The decomposition of an admissible cap functional into its normal and tangential parts gives the uniform regularization gap at most s. For a general norm-one reference, the same skew map yields the universal index upper bound by orthogonality and the contraction of its normalized reference slopes. Strict cap boundaries are handled through suprema. The scalar case evaluates directly. The finite diagnostic returned 20136 successful checks, but proofs are analytic.

value.rationale: The finite-tolerance radius is part of the standard definition used to construct numerical indices, but previous work mostly sends its tolerance to zero. Here the optimal positive finite-tolerance index and the sharp error of that limiting process are determined simultaneously for every metric space embedded isometrically in a real Hilbert target, regardless of cardinality and dimension. The formula has exact square-root asymptotics, a scalar-versus-vector dimension jump, a universal extension to nonisometric references on one side, and explicit sharp witnesses. It supplies quantitative information not contained in qualitative vanishing results and does not depend on arbitrary selected numerical examples.
